summary: Zero CRIT. One MAJ (executable bit unverifiable from read artifacts — requires operator confirmation before merge, trivial one-command resolution). Two MIN, three nits. All 11 verifiable AC items pass; AC(xii)–(xiv) correctly process-pending. TF-020P-003/004/005 closure paths are satisfied. ADOPT-001 §12.7.9.1 is present and accurate. STATUS.md strikethrough-and-✅ pattern matches convention. scp-policy-check and scp-pre-push-verify.sh have complementary non-overlapping scopes. No cross-repo closure items required.

findings.finding: AC(i) explicitly requires chmod +x. The ADOPT-001 §12.7.9.1 usage example shows scripts/scp-pre-push-verify.sh without a bash prefix, which requires mode 100755 in git. File read cannot confirm git-tracked permissions. If the executable bit is absent the invocation pattern shown in ADOPT-001 fails with permission denied, breaking the slice primary UX claim.
findings.impact: If mode is not 100755, operators following ADOPT-001 §12.7.9.1 verbatim get a permission-denied error. The fix is one command: git update-index --chmod=+x scripts/scp-pre-push-verify.sh. No design rework required — verify before merge.
findings.remediation: Operator: run git ls-files --stage scripts/scp-pre-push-verify.sh and confirm the mode prefix is 100755. If it shows 100644, fix with git update-index --chmod=+x scripts/scp-pre-push-verify.sh and amend the commit. Does not require a full fix-round; single-operator verification before PR merge is sufficient.

findings.finding: §12.7.9 (Pre-commit hook — optional, recommended) targets downstream adopters installing scp-policy-check as a pre-commit hook in their own repos. §12.7.9.1 (Rule-author pre-push verify wrapper) targets SCP-internal rule authors modifying policies/SCP-R-*.rego. These are different audiences with different workflows. Placing a SCP-internal tooling section as a sub-section of an adopter-facing section mixes audiences. Arguments FOR: both sections are pre-push local-dev gates — conceptual proximity is real; a reader of §12.7.9 will naturally encounter §12.7.9.1 and understand the distinction; the post-TF-020P-005 parenthetical in the title signals its provenance. Arguments AGAINST: an adopter skimming §12.7.9 may be confused by a sub-section that says if you are authoring SCP-R-NNN rule files — a workflow that is irrelevant to them; a dedicated §12.x SCP rule author tooling section would avoid the mixing.
findings.impact: Low. The section is accurate and discoverable. Audience mixing is a clarity concern, not a governance gap. No adopter action is misdirected by the placement.
findings.remediation: Acceptable as-is for v1.1.0. File as TF-020P-005b-candidate: Consider moving §12.7.9.1 to a dedicated SCP rule-author tooling section (e.g. a new §12.7.x reserved for SCP-self tooling) as part of the next ADOPT-001 structural pass (opportunistic, no deadline).

A rule author following the inline reference lands at §12.7.9 (the adopter pre-commit hook section) and must find §12.7.9.1 as a child. Still discoverable, but the reference is imprecise.

findings.criterion: Version-parity warning non-fatal — forward TF candidacy
findings.finding: DISPATCH-NOTE Risk Surface §1 acknowledges that non-fatal version-parity warnings could allow a version-drifted operator to get local-pass/CI-fail false-pass scenarios. The risk is acknowledged but not filed as a tracked-forward item. A configurable severity mode (env var SCP_PRE_PUSH_VERSION_STRICT=1 to make the parity check fatal) would address workflows where strict parity is desired without changing the default behaviour.
findings.impact: Low. The non-fatal default is the right posture for most operators. The risk is bounded — CI remains authoritative. The warning is visible in stderr output.
findings.remediation: File as TF-020P-005c-candidate (low priority): Add optional SCP_PRE_PUSH_VERSION_STRICT=1 env var to make .tool-versions parity check fatal — for CI-in-CI or strict local-dev workflows. Closure: opportunistic, file if a second requestor surfaces the need.

operator_usage_gap_assessment.rationale: The DISPATCH-NOTE correctly files git pre-push hook installation OUT. Reasons: (1) .git/hooks/ is per-clone state, not committable — any install the hook step is user-specific and cannot be enforced at repo level; (2) a forced pre-push hook affects ALL pushes, creating friction for non-rule-author contributors; (3) the usage pattern is simple enough that ADOPT-001 §12.7.9.1 guidance is sufficient; (4) the cost of an occasional forgotten pre-push run is one CI roundtrip per slip — acceptable at current team size; (5) a future adopter-feedback-driven TF can address this if the friction proves real. The Pre-push hook installer slice candidate TF is correctly characterised as contingent on adopter feedback.

tf_020p_005a_candidacy_assessment.rationale: The wrapper CI-parity claim is validated by CI itself. Every PR modifying policies/SCP-R-*.rego exercises all three wrapper gates through CI. If the wrapper diverges from CI (e.g. a flag drift in the Regal disable list), the next policy-modifying PR will catch it when CI fails but the wrapper passed. A bats smoke-test would only test the wrapper against its own logic — it would NOT detect CI-parity divergence (the only meaningful failure mode). The only additional value a smoke-test provides is shell-quoting or bash-version regression detection, which is low probability given the script simplicity and bash 3.2 compatibility claim. The DISPATCH-NOTE reasoning is correct.

cross_repo_closure_items.rationale: scp-pre-push-verify.sh operates on policies/SCP-R-*.rego files within the SCP repo only. CT, mapp-estate-regression, and ACC are downstream adopters; they do not author SCP-R-*.rego rule files. No cross-repo documentation, tooling, or notification changes are required for this slice.
